hpi_details: 29M with lateral joint-line knee pain and catching; clarify onset, twisting trauma, true locking, swelling, and ability to bear weight.
ideas: He thinks he might have pulled a tendon or chipped a small piece of bone when he twisted his knee during a weekend soccer match.
concerns: He is worried that he might need invasive knee surgery and won't be able to play in his rec league championship game next month.
expectations: He hopes to get an MRI scan today to see what is clicking inside and get a supportive knee brace.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Lateral meniscus tear evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Lateral meniscus tear is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Lateral Meniscus Tear: Knee MRI, physical therapy, arthroscopic partial meniscectomy, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Lateral meniscus tear.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to ACL tear without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Mechanical catching/locking suggests displaced tear fragment.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of knee pain along lateral joint line with catching sound. HPI: meniscal cartilage tear.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Lateral Meniscus Tear.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Lateral Meniscus Tear.
reference_soap.plan: Perform focused examination and obtain radiographs when fracture, osteoarthritis, or another bony cause is a concern; reserve MRI for persistent symptoms or when results will guide management. Begin activity modification and rehabilitation as appropriate. Prompt orthopedic assessment is needed for a true locked knee; if surgery is considered, repair/preservation versus partial meniscectomy depends on tear pattern and patient factors.

must_ask.say: Can you describe the catching or clicking feeling in your knee?
Does your knee ever get stuck and unable to fully straighten?
How did this knee pain start — any twisting injury?
Can you point to exactly where along the outside of your knee it hurts?

must_ask.objective: Explain the MRI and treatment options
must_ask.say: If symptoms and examination support a meniscal injury, MRI may help guide treatment. Options range from rehabilitation to specialist discussion of meniscus-preserving surgery when appropriate.

history.answer: The outer side of my right knee has been hurting, and it makes this clicking or catching sound whenever I bend it.
It is just my right knee, specifically along the outer side; my left knee and other joints feel completely fine.
It started 5 days ago right after I twisted my knee playing basketball, and the soreness has gradually worsened since.
It feels like a deep dull ache at rest, but it turns into a sharp 6 out of 10 pain when I squat or twist my leg.
There was some mild swelling that showed up the next morning, but the knee never turned red or felt hot.
It feels a bit stiff for maybe 5 to 10 minutes when I get out of bed, but it eases up quickly once I start moving.
Bending it deeply, going down stairs, and pivoting make it hurt more; resting and keeping an ice pack on it helps.
I can walk and put weight on it, but going down stairs is awkward, and sudden turning causes a sharp twinge.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
I landed awkwardly and twisted my right knee while turning for a rebound during a pickup basketball game 5 days ago.
Yes, I felt a distinct pop along the outer edge of my knee when I twisted it on the court.
It frequently clicks and feels like something catches inside when I bend it past ninety degrees, but it has not locked up solid where I cannot straighten it.
No, the knee does not buckle or give way under me, it just catches and aches.
No, I have never injured this knee or had problems with any other joint before.
I felt a bit worn out and tired over the last few days because the discomfort kept waking me up, but I have not had unexplained weight loss.
No, I do not have any skin rashes, mouth ulcers, hair thinning, red eyes, or dry mouth.
No, I have no morning back stiffness, heel soreness, or sausage-like swelling in my toes or fingers.
No recent diarrhea, burning when I urinate, genital discharge, or sore throat.
I drink one or two beers on weekends; I do not eat excess red meat or seafood, and I do not take water pills.
No, I have never had steroid injections, knee surgery, or artificial implants.
I have been in a monogamous relationship with my girlfriend for two years, and there are no new sexual partners.
I was playing soccer over the weekend and twisted awkwardly, so I thought I might have pulled a tendon or chipped a piece of bone in there.
I'm really worried this means I'll need surgery and have to sit out of our championship tournament next month.
I'm hoping to get an MRI to see what's making that clicking sound and maybe get a good brace so I can walk normally.
No chronic illnesses; I have always been healthy without high blood pressure or diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I have taken over-the-counter ibuprofen a couple of times over the last few days, which slightly dulls the ache, but no other medicines.
No known allergies to any medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink socially, maybe one or two beers a couple of times a month.
I work as an office accountant sitting at a desk, and I live in an apartment with an elevator.
No one in my family has rheumatoid arthritis, gout, or early joint problems.

exam.finding: Alert, well-nourished young man sitting comfortably on the examination table without acute distress.
Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.

Right knee has mild effusion without erythema or warmth; focal tenderness along the lateral joint line; McMurray test produces a painful palpable click on external rotation with valgus stress; negative Lachman, anterior/posterior drawer, and varus/valgus stress tests; left knee is normal.
No rashes, malar rash, psoriatic plaques, tophi, or nail changes noted.
Calves are soft, non-tender, and symmetrical without swelling or cords.
Distal pulses including dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally with normal capillary refill.
Slightly antalgic gait favoring the right lower limb, avoiding forceful pivoting or deep flexion on the right knee.
